# Public API

Import RelFlow as `import relflow as rf`. This page maps the public API to its
reference pages. For a first payment model, start with
[Getting Started](../getting-started.qmd).

## Common workflow

Define the payment fields, provide training and validation data, then fit and
predict. The application supplies the Parquet files shown below. Training and
validation records include `disputed`; prediction requests can omit it.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
datamodule = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train="payments/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/validation.parquet",
)
model.fit(datamodule, batch_size=128, max_epochs=20)
prediction_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    predict="payments/requests.parquet",
)
predictions = model.predict(datamodule=prediction_data, batch_size=256, devices=1)
```

`mask=True` declares the prediction target. Fitting restores the best validation
checkpoint by default. Predictions are returned as an Arrow table.
[Prediction output](../guides/prediction-output.qmd) uses nested field
names for decoded results and a separate column for requested representations.

## Build a model

| API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `rf.Model.xs`, `.sm`, `.md`, `.lg`, `.xl` | Build from fields with capacity defaults for the root, child branches, and leaf decoders; explicit node settings take precedence. |
| `rf.Model(...)` | Build with explicit dimensions from named fields and branches, or accept an existing `rf.Schema`. |
| `rf.Branch(...)` | Group repeated transaction records into a local context. |
| `rf.Boolean`, `rf.Number`, `rf.Category` | Represent a dispute outcome, payment amount, or merchant label. |
| `rf.Enum`, `rf.Set`, `rf.DateParts` | Represent declared currency codes, merchant tags, or booking calendar parts. |
| `rf.Hash`, `rf.Quantile`, `rf.Text`, `rf.Vector`, `rf.Cluster` | Represent identifier equality, numeric percentiles, text, supplied vectors, or learned label groups. |
| `rf.Attention`, `rf.Mean` | Choose branch reduction; `reduction=None` preserves routed tokens. |
| `rf.Mask`, `rf.Jitter` | Configure visibility/objectives and continuous input perturbation. |

See [Data Types](../core-concepts/data-types.qmd),
[Model Tree](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd), and
[Size Presets](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd#choose-a-size).
Constructor options live with their owning type.

## Train and evaluate

| API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `rf.ArrowDataModule` | Provide named splits from Arrow tables, files, datasets, or restartable Arrow factories. |
| `rf.PolarsDataModule` | Convert eager DataFrames once into the Arrow pipeline. |
| `rf.DuckDBDataModule` | Read restartable Arrow batches from configured DuckDB queries. |
| `rf.source` | Configure Arrow file reading. |
| `rf.preprocess`, `rf.Preprocessor` | Transform eager Polars frames before binding data. |
| `rf.adamw` | Build an AdamW factory for custom or native Lightning workflows. |
| `model.fit` | Configure AdamW and train a data module with automatic hardware selection, early stopping, and best-checkpoint rollback. |
| `model.validate`, `model.test` | Evaluate the corresponding data-module split and return aggregate metrics. |
| `model.track` | Log a custom metric through Lightning; training defaults to step logging and evaluation to pass aggregates. |
| `rf.EarlyStopping`, `rf.RollbackCheckpoint` | Configure stopping and best-checkpoint restoration explicitly. |
| `model.compile` | Compile selected encoders and attention pools; returns the same model. |

`rf.CustomDataModule` and `rf.SyntheticDataModule` support application-owned
mapping streams. Prefer Arrow and Polars modules when the data already has
that form. See [Data Modules](../guides/data-modules.qmd),
[Preprocessing](../guides/preprocessors.qmd),
[Training And Checkpoints](../guides/lightning.qmd),
[Evaluation](../guides/evaluation.qmd), and
[Performance](../guides/performance.qmd).
For an unlabeled training objective followed by a labeled task, see
[Pretraining And Fine-Tuning](../guides/pretraining.qmd).

## Predict and save

| API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `model.predict` | Return an Arrow prediction table, with optional batch sizing for direct input or a prediction data module. |
| `model.save`, `rf.Model.load` | Save and restore the schema and learned model state. |
| `rf.Writer` | Write Lightning prediction batches to rank-partitioned Parquet files. |
| `rf.postprocess`, `rf.Postprocessor` | Transform eager Polars frames after prediction writing. |
| `rf.Deployment` | Serve models through the optional HTTP runtime. |

Serving types, including `rf.Accelerator`, `rf.JSONBackend`, and
`rf.ModelSource`, require `relflow[serving]`. See
[Prediction Output](../guides/prediction-output.qmd),
[Postprocessors](../guides/postprocessors.qmd), and [Serving](../guides/serving.qmd).

## Advanced schema operations

| API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `rf.Address`, `rf.where`, `rf.predicate` | Address and select schema nodes, such as `rf.Address("trxns", "amount")`. |
| `model.select`, `update`, `extend`, `delete`, `reset`, `override` | Inspect or change the schema. |
| `rf.presets.factory` | Bind an immutable preset configuration to a typed classmethod on a `Model` subclass. |
| `model.encode`, `model.forward`, `model.write` | Access the encoding, Torch computation, and Arrow writing stages. |

See [Schema Mutation](../guides/schema-mutation.qmd) and
[Model Tree](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd) before changing a fitted model.

## Extensions

`rf.Extension` registers a datatype's request, tensorfield, embedder, decoder,
output, and related behavior. `rf.RequestBase`, `rf.TensorFieldBase`,
`rf.EmbedderBase`, `rf.DecoderBase`, `rf.TensorInput`, `rf.Context`, and
`rf.RaggedField` provide its shared contracts. See
[Custom Tensorfields](../guides/custom-tensorfields.qmd).
